pages.text: $(thing)Air curing$() is the slowest and simplest method. The rack must not be getting rained on, and sky light at the block above the rack must be at least $(item)8$().
Air curing requires $(item)72,000 ticks$(), or about $(item)3 Minecraft days$() of valid air-curing time. The timer only advances while the requirements remain valid.
pages.title: Time
Fan-Assisted Air Cure
pages.text: With $(thing)Create$(), plain Encased Fan airflow reaching a wooden rack provides accelerated Air Curing. The fan is an alternative valid airflow source, not a different cure type. If normal Sun Curing conditions are valid, the same plain airflow accelerates Sun Curing instead.

pages.title: Hanging Bunches
pages.text: Traditional hanging bunches naturally Air Cure under a continuous roof when no side opening qualifies for Sun Curing. Their support block above does not need to expose the bunch to vertical sky.

Covered outdoor racks are useful because air curing does not require direct sky access. Just make sure the cover does not reduce sky light below 8. If another curing method becomes valid, the rack can switch methods and the final batch may count as mixed.
